summary: Nalini Balbir is an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Colette Caillat (~1977–1980). She held posts at INALCO (~1982–1988), Sorbonne Nouvelle University as Professor (~1988), and École Pratique des Hautes Études as Directeur d'études (~2000).

Nalini Devdas is a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. She completed her PhD at Concordia University in 2004 under Leslie Orr, having also studied under teachers including Steven Collins and Richard P. Hayes. She held a post at Carleton University.

Nam-lin Hur is a historian of Japan and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and earned his PhD at Princeton (~1992) under Helen Hardacre. He held posts at Harvard (~1992–1993) and the University of British Columbia (~1996).

Naman P. Ahuja is an Indologist and art historian who earned a doctorate at SOAS University of London (~2001). Around 2001, he became Professor of Indian Art and Architecture at Jawaharlal Nehru University.
Namita Das specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at Gauhati University in 2012 under the supervision of Sibnath Sarma.

Namkhai Norbu was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Derge Gonchen Monastery, Kuse Serjong Shedra, and Khamdre Shedra. He taught at Southwest Minzu University (1954) and held professorships at the University of Naples from 1964.

Nancy Ammerman is a religious studies scholar who studied at Southwest Baptist University, University of Louisville, and Yale University (1983). She held positions at Emory University (1984–1995), Hartford International University (1995–2003), and Boston University (2003).

Nancy Grace Lin specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She undertook graduate studies at Columbia University (~2001–2004) and completed her PhD at the University of California, Berkeley (~2004–2011), working with scholars including Robert A. F. Thurman and Jacob Dalton.

Nancy Hock is a scholar of art history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of California, Berkeley (~1978–1987) under Joanna Gottfried Williams and held a post at the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco (~1986–1994).

Nancy McCagney works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied under figures including Chögyam Trungpa, Ninian Smart, Gerald James Larson, and William F. Powell (~1985–1994). She held a post at the University of Delaware around 1994.

Nandini Bhattacharyya-Panda works in history, archaeology, and Indology. She has held posts as a Project Fellow at the Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute of Asian Studies and as a Senior Fellow at the Indian Council of Historical Research.

Nanigopal Majumdar was an archaeologist and Indologist. He served as Superintendent at the Archaeological Survey of India in 1931 and as Superintendent of the Archaeological Section at the Indian Museum from around 1932 to 1938.

Naoji Okuyama is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University (~1980–1985), where he worked as an assistant and lecturer (~1985–1990), and became a professor at Koyasan University around 2002.
Naoki Nabeshima is a Buddhist studies scholar who founded Ryukoku University, where he served as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies.
Naoko Nishimura is an Indology and linguistics scholar. She earned her PhD at Tohoku University (~1997–2002) under Toshifumi Goto and held an appointment there as a specialized researcher.

Naomi Appleton is a Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies scholar. She earned a D.Phil. at Oxford (~2005–2008) under Christopher Minkowski and David Gellner, holding fellowships at Cardiff University (~2009–2012) and the University of Edinburgh (~2012).

Naoshiro Tsuji was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Tokyo and Oxford. He served as Associate Professor at the University of Tokyo (1927–1960), held a post at Keio (1960), and directed Toyo Bunko (~1974–1979).

Naoya Funahashi is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shoko Takeuchi. He was a research fellow with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science and held a post at Otani University from circa 1974 to 2009.
Narada Mahathera was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Pelene Siri Vajirañāṇa around 1916 and attended Ceylon University College around 1921.

Narayan Hemandas Samtani is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He earned his PhD at the University of Delhi (1957–1961), where he was a Research Fellow, and was appointed Lecturer in Pali at Banaras Hindu University in 1971.
